## 3. The evidence that moved it




**Nature Medicine declares a benchmarking crisis in biomedical machine
learning** ([40200055](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40200055/)). This is the
single most consequential card in the first half of 2025, and it is the origin
of a claim the corpus later had to correct: April was recorded as the high-water
mark of negative clinical-AI evidence on the strength of "null randomized trials
plus a benchmarking-crisis editorial". The editorial is real. The null randomized
trials never existed — re-reading every month of 2025 under one rule found zero
titles stating a null for any AI intervention.

**And in the same month, the audit reaches the models themselves.**
[40251685](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40251685/) (*Genome Biol*): zero-shot
evaluation reveals limitations of single-cell foundation models. Read with the
benchmarking-crisis editorial, April 2025 is when the methods literature began
auditing the thing it had spent the previous year building — eight months before
this corpus recorded that as having happened.

**"Virtual cell" enters the corpus here**, in a *Nature Biotechnology* title
([40229360](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40229360/), virtual cells for
predictive immunotherapy) — two months *before* the *Cell* challenge that names
the concept, and seven months before the phrase reaches the methods journals.

**An intracellular checkpoint reaches first-in-human.**
[40315882](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40315882/) (*Lancet Oncol*): CRISPR-Cas9
CISH-edited T cells in metastatic colorectal cancer. Note the shape — the target
is not blocked with an antibody, it is deleted in the cell being infused. That
manoeuvre becomes the class's main survival route by 2026.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[40249828](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40249828/) (*Sci Immunol*):
**CCR8-positive decidual regulatory T cells maintain maternal-fetal immune
tolerance in early pregnancy.** CCR8 is the marker chosen for effector-Treg
depletion precisely because it is supposed to be tumour-restricted. This is the
earliest and most direct card in the corpus against that premise, and it sits at
the head of a series — a CCR4-directed depleting bispecific selling itself on
avoiding systemic toxicity in December, and opposing Treg subsets in colorectal
cancer in the new year.

[40202509](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40202509/): neutrophil MYO1F is
*required* for the response to checkpoint blockade.
[40306958](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40306958/): tumour-infiltrating mast
cells act as a chemoimmunotherapy *enhancer*.
[40139186](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40139186/): metallophilic marginal zone
macrophages cross-prime protective CD8 immunity against blood-borne tumours.

Against them, [40280128](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40280128/) is the
thread's clearest support: Treg depletion promotes myeloid activation and
glioblastoma response to anti-PD-1. Both directions are real, which is the point
of carding stance rather than topic.

[39786370](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39786370/): non-selective
beta-adrenergic blockade impairs haematopoietic regeneration after transplant in
mice *and humans*, with a companion editorial titled "Don't Lose Your Nerve".
Filed as a refutation on the neuro-immune thread — the same adrenergic axis the
thread's supports are built on, cutting the other way in a clinical setting.

### (b) Method credibility

[40205439](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40205439/): the standard
high-mitochondrial-content quality filter depletes viable, metabolically altered
malignant cells from cancer single-cell studies. A default QC step that
systematically removes the cells of interest.

[40197327](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40197327/): missing cell types in
single-cell references distort bulk deconvolution.
[40082610](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40082610/): feature selection method
choice changes integration and querying performance.
[40240607](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40240607/) (*Nature*): there is low
overlap between transcription factor DNA binding and regulatory targets — which
undercuts binding-derived regulatory networks generally.
